About us

Vaultless design


AuthNull delivers a vaultless design by using decentralized identity standard. No vaults to manage, secure or replicate. Credentials are issued by an Issuer, and verified by a verifier using Public Key infrastructure and ED25519 crytographic signatures. Credentials are stored and managed by users on their wallets.


How does this work?



Frequently
asked questions

Answers to the most frequently asked questions.

Decentralized identity is a type of identity management that allows people to control their own digital identity without depending on a specific service provider. Each user can store and manage their own credentials by a public / private key pair that has been issued for each user by an organization.

Each organizion has an Issuer - an entity that verifies user identities and generates a public / private key pair for for each user. The private key is stored in the wallet Users are issued a wallet when they are onboarded to organizations. This is done after verifying identity.

All credentials are stored in a decentralized wallet as opposed to being in a secret store.

If your organization has a credential policy, then all credentials - passwordless credentials, SSH Keys and Passwords are rotated and automatically shipped to respective assigned user's wallets.

Passwordless credentials (also called as Verified credentials - VCs), SSH Keys and Passwords are the kinds of credentials that are stored in the vault.

All credentials issued to users' wallets are automatically revoked when the users are removed from an Identity solution as a part of the Join-Manage-Leave (JML) Lifecycle. Additionally, administrators can force revoke, expire existing wallets as well as credentials.

As a part of the checkout process, previous credentials are expired and new credentials are issued. This means the users who previously held credentials in their vault will see it become inaccessible and the new users will get credential notifications.
